messages.subject: nimbleSMC example producing NaNs?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to use pMCMC for a project I'm working on and wanted to use nimble. To understand the functionality I have been trying out the pMCMC example in the Nimble User Guide (pg 100). However, when I try to compile and then run the example, I get a posterior full of NaNs. Any idea what is going on here? 

This is the code I am using (the last three lines were written by myself so perhaps the error is there?):

library(nimbleSMC)
timeModelCode <- nimbleCode({
  x[1] ~ dnorm(mu_0, 1)
  y[1] ~ dnorm(x[1], 1)
  for(i in 2:t){
    x[i] ~ dnorm(x[i-1] * a + b, 1)
    y[i] ~ dnorm(x[i] * c, 1)
  }
  a ~ dunif(0, 1)
  b ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  c ~ dnorm(1,1)
  mu_0 ~ dnorm(0, 1)
})
# simulate some data
t <- 25; mu_0 <- 1
x <- rnorm(1 ,mu_0, 1)
y <- rnorm(1, x, 1)
a <- 0.5; b <- 1; c <- 1
for(i in 2:t){
  x[i] <- rnorm(1, x[i-1] * a + b, 1)
  y[i] <- rnorm(1, x[i] * c, 1)
}

# build the model
inits <- list(a = 0.5, b = 1, c = 1, mu_0 = 1)
rTimeModel <- nimbleModel(timeModelCode, constants = list(t = t),
                          data <- list(y = y), inits = inits)
cTimeModel <- compileNimble(rTimeModel)
timeConf <- configureMCMC(rTimeModel) 
timeConf$addSampler(target = c("a", "b", "c", "mu_0"), type = "RW_PF_block",
                    control = list(propCov= diag(4), adaptScaleOnly = FALSE,
                                   latents = "x", pfOptimizeNparticles = TRUE))

timeConfMCMC <- buildMCMC(timeConf)
compiled_model <- compileNimble(rTimeModel, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
compiled_model_MCMC <- compileNimble(timeConfMCMC, project = rTimeModel, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

resultsLinear <- runMCMC(compiled_model_MCMC,
                         niter = 10000,
                         nburnin = 1000,
                         inits = inits)

Many thanks,
Debbie

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: nimbleSMC example producing NaNs?
parts:
Hi Debbie,

Thanks for posting this issue.  Yikes, I see two things going on from our example code.

In order to use the pMCMC sampler, normally all other samplers should be removed (or not assigned in the first place).  The state of the model from the pMCMC does not necessarily make sense for other samplers.  Our example code omitted that.  The two ways to do it would be:
timeConf <- configureMCMC(rTimeModel, nodes=NULL)
or (equivalently)
timeConf <- configureMCMC(rTimeModel)
timeConf$removeSamplers()

Because you add the RW_PF (pMCMC) sampler, you can safely ignore the warning about unsampled nodes.  Those are the latent states, and they will be handled by the PF.

The next thing I noticed is that the algorithm for automated determination of PF sample size does not work well in this case. It seems to go to small sample sizes and very poor mixing.  Please try this instead:

timeConf$addSampler(target = c("a", "b", "c", "mu_0"), type = "RW_PF_block",
                    control = list(propCov= diag(4), adaptScaleOnly = FALSE,

latents = "x", pfNparticles = 500))

With these changes, the example seems to run reasonably.  There's not much data to inform parameter estimates, but it's just a small toy data set.

I'll update these in our User Manual.

Perry
